notes.text: For more than 4, roast the quail on two sheet pans, one on each middle rack, swapping them halfway.

move.title: Flatten it, glaze it, roast it hot
move.body: Quail are small, clean birds, and Persian cooks roast them with sour-sweet pomegranate molasses and warm spices. You'll spatchcock eight quail, cutting out the backbone and pressing each bird flat, so they roast evenly in 15 minutes at high heat. They're served over a bulgur pilaf with herbs.

why.title: Out with the backbone
why.body: Spatchcocking means cutting out the backbone with shears and pressing the bird flat. A flat bird has no thick middle hiding inside a hollow cavity, so the legs and breast finish at the same time.

why.title: Thaw in the fridge
why.body: Most quail are sold frozen. A day in the fridge thaws them all the way through, so they roast evenly; a bird icy in the middle stays raw there while the outside dries.

why.title: A glaze that clings
why.body: Pomegranate molasses is pomegranate juice boiled down to a thick, tart syrup. Mixed with oil and spices, it clings to the skin and browns quickly at high heat, so it goes on in two coats.

why.title: Small bird, high heat
why.body: A quail weighs about 4 ounces. At 450°F it browns outside in the same 12 to 15 minutes it takes to cook through, which a lower oven can't do.

why.title: Quail at 165°F
why.body: All poultry is 165°F in this app. On a quail, check the thickest part of the breast from the side, close to the bone.

wrong.fix: It went on too thick or too early. Brush on the second coat only for the last 5 minutes.

wrong.sign: The legs are done but the breast isn't
wrong.fix: The bird wasn't pressed flat enough. Press harder on the breastbone next time.

wrong.sign: The quail is still icy inside
wrong.fix: It wasn't fully thawed. Roast 3 more minutes and check again.
Too much liquid. Next time, use the exact amount and don't stir while it soaks.

choices: Cut out the backbone and press the bird flat
A small bird browns outside in the time it takes to cook through

steps.text: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the upper third. Line the sheet pan with foil.
Mince the garlic and stir it into the pomegranate molasses, oil, cinnamon, cumin, and pepper in the small bowl. Pour half into a second bowl for the second coat.
Check that the quail are thawed: no ice in the cavity. Don't rinse them.
Lay each bird breast down. Cut along both sides of the backbone with the shears and lift it out. Turn the bird over and press the breastbone until it cracks flat. Pat dry and salt both sides.
steps.look: Eight flat birds, legs out to the sides.

steps.text: Freeze the backbones for stock. Wash your hands, the shears, and the board with hot, soapy water.
Lay the birds skin side up on the pan with the tongs and brush them with the first half of the glaze.
Wash the brush, the tongs, and your hands. Throw out any glaze left in the first bowl.
Bring the broth, butter, and the pilaf's salt to a boil in the saucepan. Stir in the bulgur, cover, and take it off the heat to soak while the quail roast.
Roast, then brush with the second coat and roast until deep brown.
Check the thickest breast, from the side, near the bone: at least 165°F. If not, roast 2 minutes more.
Fluff the bulgur with the fork into the medium bowl, and gently stir in the parsley, mint, and the lemon's juice.
Serve two quail per person over the pilaf, with the pan juices spooned on top.
